blocks.content: runc is the lowest-level piece of the chain, a small, focused command-line tool whose entire job is creating the actual isolated process, using namespaces and cgroups, that becomes a running container.

Given an OCI bundle (a filesystem plus a configuration describing exactly what namespaces, cgroups, and process to start), runc does exactly one thing: it creates that isolated process, this is the literal, final step where everything covered in this module's Namespaces and cgroups topics is actually applied.

blocks.alt: The final step where namespaces and cgroups are actually applied

blocks.content: 2. runc Starts It, Then Gets Out of the Way
blocks.text: 2. runc Starts It, Then Gets Out of the Way

blocks.content: Unlike containerd, runc does not stay running to supervise the container afterward, it starts the container's process and then exits, ongoing supervision is handed off to containerd-shim, covered in the containerd topic, a deliberately narrow, single-purpose design.

blocks.alt: A brief, single-purpose job, not a long-running supervisor

blocks.content:
# Roughly what happens under the hood for one docker run
runc create <container-id>
runc start <container-id>
# runc's job is done, containerd-shim now supervises the process

blocks.content: 3. Built to a Standard, Not a Docker Invention
blocks.text: 3. Built to a Standard, Not a Docker Invention

blocks.content: runc is the reference implementation of the OCI Runtime Specification, an open standard describing exactly what a container runtime must do, this is precisely the mechanism that lets an image built by Docker run correctly under a completely different tool that also honors the same spec.

blocks.alt: An implementation of an open standard, not a private Docker mechanism

blocks.content: 4. Alternative Runtimes Plug in the Same Way
blocks.text: 4. Alternative Runtimes Plug in the Same Way

blocks.content: Because the interface is standardized, runc is not the only option, alternatives like gVisor (which adds an extra sandboxing layer, intercepting syscalls for stronger isolation) or Kata Containers (which runs each container inside its own lightweight VM) can be swapped in, giving stronger isolation guarantees at some added overhead, without changing anything about how images or the rest of the stack work.

blocks.alt: Different isolation tradeoffs, same interchangeable interface

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: runc is the small, narrowly-scoped tool that actually creates a container's isolated process from namespaces and cgroups, then exits, handing supervision to containerd-shim.
It implements the open OCI Runtime Spec, which is exactly why alternative runtimes like gVisor or Kata Containers can be swapped in for stronger isolation when needed.
